newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TEICHMANN LOOKING TO REPEAT HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TEICHMANN LOOKING TO REPEAT HISTORY.

text.p: Springbok captain Gary Teichmann is hoping his side can repeat their efforts of last year against the All Blacks by winning the final test of the three-match series against the British Lions on Saturday.

"We had the same situation last year against Sean Fitzpatrick's side when we were 2-0 down in the series and we came back to win that last game. We now want to do exactly the same against the Lions and really get on a high for this year's Tri-Nations," Teichmann said on Thursday.

Yet, although Ellis Park has proved to be a relatively successful hunting-ground for South Africa since their re-admission to the international game in 1992, Teichmann refuses to rely on superstition.
"We're not going to rely on the history of Ellis Park because I know the Lions will be out to get a 3-0 series result. It'll be a hard game and we'll take it as a normal test match."
South Africa have won their last six tests at Ellis Park after narrow defeats there at the hands of New Zealand in 1992 and France in 1993.
But, if South Africa are to win against the Lions in Johannesburg on Saturday, Teichmann knows his side have to be a lot more disciplined with regard to penalties.
"We've had a good look at our performance in Durban last weekend and there are a number of the decisions that we weren't happy with. But you've got to accept it," Teichmann said.
"We are not at all happy with the amount of penalties we're giving away. You know, 17 penalties in a test game is ridiculous and there were a number of times that the decisions were correct.
"That's what we've got to look at. Even in their half, we would be right up in attack -- then you give a penalty away and you're suddenly back in defence."

South Africa's other crucial problem at Kings Park last Saturday was the total absence of a successful goal-kicker. Henry Honiball, Percy Montgomery and Andre Joubert missed six attempts between them but Teichmann believes new cap Jannie de Beer will plug this gap at Ellis Park.
"He's shown that he's a great goal-kicker but I think he's also got to fill in the areas where Henry Honiball was great -- that's where he's going to look at his game to improve."
Teichmann is confident the 26-year-old Free State fly-half will slot into the Springbok playing pattern with minimal fuss.

"The way that we play, I think he'll be able to fit in -- it all depends on the kind of ball that the forwards are giving the backs. If you're giving good, quick possession, then he'll be running flat onto the ball and he can spread it wide.
"So it's up to us forwards to give him the quick ball to make the decisions on how he wants to play the game."
Despite dominating both territory and possession in Durban during the second test, South Africa failed to get more than a score ahead of the Lions at any stage.
As a result, many criticised the Springboks for their relative lack of vision and flair -- criticism which Teichmann feels is unjustified.
"Well, we scored three tries to none in Durban, so at least our backs were scoring. I don't really see how people can say that our three-quarter play was unimaginative."
